This bear had to tell the internet she wasn't a person in a costume.
Hangzhou Zoo, summer twenty twenty-three. A video shows Angela, a sun bear, standing on two legs like a person, looking straight at the crowd.
Her fur hangs in loose folds. Like a baggy suit.
People online decide: that's a man in a bear suit.
Why would anyone believe that? Because Chinese zoos had history.
In twenty thirteen, a zoo in Henan put a Tibetan mastiff in the lion cage. Visitors heard it bark.
In twenty twenty-four, a zoo in Jiangsu showed off panda dogs. They were chow chows, dyed black and white.
So the Hangzhou zoo answered, posting as Angela: people just don't understand sun bears.
Sun bears are the smallest bears in the world. Their loose skin lets them twist around and bite back if something grabs them.
And the zoo added: no person could last in that fur in the summer heat.
Visitors poured in to check for themselves. About twenty thousand a day.
Angela is real. She just stands like us.
Would you have believed it was a person?
In China, not everything is what it looks like. See for yourself at laowai dot ma.
